classes.name: ISS33-NATIVE-ENTRY-TIMESTAMP-TRUST
classes.owner: Recorder native-session structural trust seam (`src/recorder/session.ts`, synchronized generated artifact, and its focused session-integrity test)
classes.boundary: The outer `timestamp` of every non-header Pi-v3 session entry, including the two direct package lifecycle rows; not inner message timestamps, package details, accepted presentation text, or arbitrary displayed prose
classes.disposition: Sustained. Pi-v3 session authority defines the outer `SessionEntryBase.timestamp` as a string written with `new Date().toISOString()`; this is distinct from assistant/tool-result message timestamps, which are numeric Unix milliseconds. C3 admits only direct top-level message rows carrying that native entry field, and malformed native-session evidence must fail closed. At current HEAD, `readSession()` validates canonical ISO lexical semantics only for the header, while `directIssuance()`/`directResult()` check only presence of the outer key. A direct fixed-HEAD reproduction sealed lifecycle rows with issuance `timestamp:null` and result `timestamp:{bad:true}`. Add one shared domain predicate/validator at the session seam and use it for both the header and every non-header entry: require a string whose parsed value is valid and whose `toISOString()` exactly equals the input. Malformed outer entry timestamps are native structural corruption and therefore map to `session-corrupt` before lifecycle extraction, not `acceptance-invalid`. Add only one representative malformed-entry tracer through `readSession()` to prove fail-closed behavior; existing valid sessions are the green control. Do not enumerate format permutations, duplicate validation in the extractor, validate presentation text, alter inner numeric message timestamp law, or add a production hook.

classes.name: ISS33-SECURITY-FIXTURE-NAMES
classes.owner: Focused Recorder trust-boundary tests only (`test/recorder-config-session-integrity.test.ts` and `test/native-session-sealer.test.ts`)
classes.boundary: Only the reported identifiers `raw`, `put`, `x`, `c`, `f`, `g`, and `pair`; no helper extraction, abstraction, reformatting, assertion changes, fixture redesign, or unrelated test cleanup
classes.disposition: Sustained as one bounded Mysterious Name class. These are not incidental arithmetic locals: `raw` constructs the Recorder security config, `put` writes the trusted main-session JSONL, `pair` creates a matched package lifecycle, and `x`/`c`/`f`/`g` carry mutable config or multi-field session fixtures across identity, symlink, chain, truncation, and snapshot assertions. In the current compressed tests, their meaning cannot be recovered without repeatedly expanding helper bodies and return shapes, which materially impairs review of the trust boundary. Perform identifier-only role-revealing renames, for example `recorderConfigInput`, `writeMainSessionRows`, `configInput`, `config`, `sessionFixture`, `unterminatedSessionFixture`, and `packageLifecycleRows`. Do not create abstractions or otherwise churn the tests.
